_engine_flags_comment: Qwen3.5-9B-NVFP4 needs three extras vs the router's default:
--quantization modelopt   modelopt PTQ; vLLM autodetect can
miss it on dev images.
--language-model-only     Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration
arch registers a vision tower; this
text-only quant has no vision_config
and this flag tells vLLM to skip
the encoder.
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 (override the router's default 0.92).
Needed only when MTP is enabled at
long context (>=64K): baseline at 64K
already saturates the 0.92 cap (22.08 GiB)
with KV+activations, and MTP's ~1 GiB
scaffold pushes past. At 32K the 0.92
default is sufficient -- the bump is
harmless at short ctx (vLLM uses the
larger pool for prefix caching).
Qwen3.6-27B-Text-NVFP4-MTP needs five extras vs the router's
default vllmEntrypoint emission:
--quantization modelopt   the checkpoint's quantization_config
uses NVIDIA TensorRT-Model-Optimizer's
modelopt schema; vLLM autodetect can
miss it on dev builds.
--language-model-only     architectures: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration
registers a vision tower; the `-Text-`
variant has no vision_config and this
flag tells vLLM to skip the encoder.
--max-num-seqs 4          KV pool at 32K + the MTP head's extra
verification positions fits 4 in-flight
sequences comfortably on 24G.
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 (override the router's default 0.92)
and  VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0
(env). vLLM 0.20.0's CUDA graph memory
profiler double-counts on Blackwell --
leaves only 0.71 GiB for KV at the
router's default 0.92, killing engine
init. The env var disables the profiler;
the bumped utilization gives KV room.
Gemma 4 is multi-modal (vision encoder). Without this, vLLM
errors at engine init with 'Chunked MM input disabled but
max_tokens_per_mm_item (2496) is larger than max_num_batched_tokens
(2048).' Raising the batch-token cap to 4096 clears the check
without significant VRAM impact at our typical decode batch sizes.
--enforce-eager disables CUDA graph capture, freeing the ~4 GiB
workspace vLLM otherwise pre-reserves for cudagraph buffers. The
model weights + fp8 KV cache fit comfortably in 24 GiB at 128K
context only with eager mode on; with graphs enabled, PyTorch
fails to allocate the last 316 MiB during model load. Cost: ~10-
20% throughput drop on decode (no graph batching). For 24 GiB
Blackwell that is the going trade to access 128K context.
Same CUDA-graph-workspace trade as Nemotron-3-Nano-30B (the sibling
30B MoE NVFP4 on this card). The load probe found engine init aborts
at 64K with 'ValueError: 3.0 GiB KV cache needed > 2.27 GiB
available' -- a ~0.73 GiB deficit after weights + the ~4 GiB
cudagraph workspace. --enforce-eager frees that workspace so the KV
pool fits, lifting the model past its previous 32K serve cap. Cost:
~10-20% decode throughput (no graph batching); zero correctness or
quality impact (identical kernels, just launched eagerly). Model has
max_position_embeddings=262144 native, so this is engine tuning, not
a context extension -- consistent with the as-delivered policy.

_stability_note: --generation-config vllm) were tried and REVERTED: they served fine
for single sequential requests but crash-looped the engine under the
bench harness's request pattern (model-switch + concurrency) on this
96%-full 24G card. The default sampler is stable across a request
sequence up to 1500-token outputs with no crash, and long answers
(900+ tokens) are not truncated, so --generation-config vllm is
unnecessary here. Stability over the ~24% sampler speedup.

_engine_flags_comment: DiffusionGemma is a discrete-diffusion (block-autoregressive)
encoder-decoder dLLM, served by vLLM 0.22.1+ (the gemma-cu130
image; arch DiffusionGemmaForBlockDiffusion). The ~18 GiB NVFP4
checkpoint leaves a tight budget on 24G; verified flags (direct
podman launch, real decode at 128K) vs the router default:
--quantization modelopt   modelopt NVFP4; matches the other
NVFP4 rows.
--max-num-seqs 4          per the vLLM DiffusionGemma recipe
(>4 OOMs).
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 (override the router's 0.92). The
killer is NOT the KV pool but a fixed
~1 GiB logits transient in
diffusion_gemma.py:_softcap_logits
(chunk_tokens x vocab 262144 x fp32).
Util must leave room OUTSIDE the pool
for it; 0.90 + the cap below fits.
--max-num-batched-tokens 512  THE key flag. The softcap logits
buffer is (prefill_chunk x vocab x 4B);
at the default 1024-token chunk that is
exactly 1024 MiB and engine init OOMs
regardless of context/util. Capping the
chunk to 512 halves it to ~512 MiB,
which fits. Trade-off: image inputs
(mm item up to max_soft_tokens=1120) are
constrained at this batch size -- this
row is tuned text-first on 24G.
--mm-processor-kwargs / --limit-mm-per-prompt  per the recipe.
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True  reclaims the
fragmented tail so the transient lands.
Verified to serve and DECODE at up to 256K on 24G with these
flags: KV 2.72 GiB = ~269K tokens (1.03x concurrency), 23.5/24
GiB peak. The 512 batch-token cap is what unlocks 256K -- it both
shrinks the logits transient AND cuts activation reservation,
freeing KV. Smaller ctx -> more concurrency headroom (128K ~1.95x).
